charts.name: Barbados reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: This pack found no legal chart of accounts in Barbados, and opened neither the Companies Act, Cap. 308, nor the Income Tax Act, Cap. 73: no section of either is cited. What the Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 87, s. 75 and the Value Added Tax Regulations, 1996, reg. 7 ask of a person who carries on a taxable activity is that accounts and records be kept, and the Act keeps them for 7 years after the end of the year they relate to. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of a statement of financial position and an income statement presented in the manner of IFRS for SMEs, which is a choice of this pack and not a text the country imposes. The settlement account of the VAT return (2100, refundable 1172) is distinct from the accounts the tax posts to (2101 to 2103 collected, 1170 and 1171 recoverable). See README.md

numbering.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Regulations, 1996, reg. 2(b) — a tax invoice carries 'a number assigned to the tax invoice identifying the invoice as one of a series issued by the registrant'. The text asks for a series, and does not say the series may have no gap, which is why `numbering` is `sequential` and not `gapless`; `number_format` is a convention this pack proposes

payment_terms.legal_reference: No Barbados text read for this pack sets a payment term between two businesses or a rate of interest on a commercial debt paid late: the penalty of 10 per cent and the interest of the Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 87, s. 46(4) are charges on the registrant towards the Comptroller, not a term between two businesses. `legal_payment_days` and `late_payment_reference` are empty

tax_point.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 87, s. 16(1) — a supply takes place when an invoice for it is issued, when payment is received or when the goods are made available or the services performed, 'whichever is the earliest'; s. 16(3) applies the same three triggers to a periodic payment under an agreement that provides for them. The closed vocabulary of this field has no value for three triggers at once: `earliest_of_delivery_or_payment` is the nearest and is what the rule reduces to when no invoice comes first. The other cases of s. 16 (hire purchase, sale on approval) are not modelled

einvoicing.legal_reference: No Barbados text read for this pack obliges a business to issue or accept an electronic invoice: the Value Added Tax Regulations, 1996, reg. 2 list the particulars of a tax invoice without naming a platform, a format or a Peppol profile, and the Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 87, s. 7(7) only asks a registrant to issue a tax invoice to another registrant who requests one. No Peppol authority for Barbados was looked for. `profile`, `party_scheme` and `vat_scheme` are null: there is no domestic profile to name

not_taxed.legal_reference: Not modelled, and not a finding that the service is untaxed. The Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 87, s. 7(1) taxes the supply in Barbados of goods or services by a registrant and goods imported; how a service received from a supplier abroad is declared was not found in the pages read (the Act's provisions on imported services were not located). The pack carries no code for it rather than guess a mechanism: such a purchase is entered with BB-P-EX and the user, with their accountant, accounts for any VAT owed outside the pack. See README.md
